Model checks

These test the models, not bets. They are scored on their own terms and ignore every filter.

Near-exact callsHow often a game line lands within 3 points and a prop projection within 1

Not a bet record. Before each game we write down the Vault line's margin and total, the simulation's, and every prop projection. After the final we count how often each one landed almost exactly on the result: a game margin or total within 3 points, a prop (points, rebounds, assists, 3-pointers) within 1. The sportsbooks' own numbers sit beside ours as the yardstick, scored the same way.

Forward test: four pockets, frozen Nov 2

Prop projections, within 1

Every game

Game simulationsDoes the real score land inside the simulated range?

Before each game the model plays it out thousands of times and gives a range for the final margin, the total points and each player's stats. The test: does the real result land inside the 80% range about 80% of the time? A range that is too narrow gets missed too often; one that is too wide gets hit almost every time and says little.

Advanced: do two players move together?

Props: minutes model vs simulationsIs the simple model as good as playing each game out?

The simple minutes model prices a prop as projected minutes times a per-minute rate, worked out directly (this is what Player Props uses). The test: does playing the game out 10,000 times, or only 50 times, price props any better?

A tell is something the market did on one prop. Several tells on a prop do not add up to a bet; each is graded on its own below. Context only.

Record by tell

A reference (Pinnacle, Novig, heavy Kalshi money or sharp accounts) moved a prop and a book or pick'em app still holds the old number. Context, not a bet: the Pinnacle-only backtest found no edge in chasing these.
